what_its_for: Mebendazole is used to treat intestinal worm infections, including pinworms, roundworms, whipworms, and hookworms. It works by stopping the worms from absorbing the nutrients they need to survive, which kills them.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole or chew it — either way works fine. You can take it with or without food. If you are treating pinworms, all household members and close contacts may need to be treated at the same time, even if they have no symptoms, to prevent the infection from spreading back to you.
dosing: The dose depends on the type of worm infection you have. For pinworms: one 100 mg tablet taken as a single dose. For roundworms, whipworms, or hookworms: one 100 mg tablet taken twice a day (morning and evening) for 3 days in a row. For pinworms, a second dose is often recommended 2 to 3 weeks later because pinworm eggs can survive in the environment and cause reinfection. Always follow the dose your doctor or pharmacist tells you — do not take more than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store mebendazole at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medication out of reach of children. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the packaging.
what_to_avoid: Avoid close physical contact with others while you have an active worm infection to prevent spreading it. Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water after using the bathroom and before eating. Wash all bedding, towels, underwear, and pajamas in hot water after starting treatment, especially for pinworms. Keep fingernails short and avoid scratching the anal area to reduce the risk of reinfection. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, avoid this medication if possible — talk to your doctor before taking it.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if you notice any of the following: severe stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that does not go away; signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing; unusual bruising or bleeding; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); extreme tiredness or weakness; or if your symptoms do not improve after finishing the full course of treatment or if the infection comes back.
when_it_works: Mebendazole starts working right away to kill the worms, but you may not notice immediate improvement in your symptoms. It can take a few days after finishing treatment for worms and eggs to be fully cleared from your body. For pinworm infections, itching around the bottom area may continue for up to a week after treatment as the body clears the worms. If your symptoms do not improve within a few days of finishing treatment, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Children under 2 years old: Mebendazole is generally not recommended for children under 2 years of age unless specifically directed by a doctor. Pregnant women: This medication should be avoided during pregnancy, especially during the first trimester, as it may harm the unborn baby. Talk to your doctor about safer options. Breastfeeding women: Small amounts of mebendazole may pass into breast milk. Consult your doctor before using this medication if you are breastfeeding. Elderly patients: No special dose adjustment is typically needed, but consult your doctor if you have any liver problems.
